transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

That sounds frustrating. On induction hobs, cutting out after 5-10 minutes on high power is most commonly the safety system kicking in because something has overheated. The two main possibilities are:
1. The hob's internal cooling fan has failed or the vents are blocked, causing the whole unit to overheat.
2. A specific zone's power module is overheating, often due to using pans that are too small for the zone or not suitable for induction. To narrow this down quickly: does the display show an error code when it switches off? Also, is your hob a ceramic/glass top (radiant) or an induction model?
its induction, samsung. a small code flashes sometimes but i didnt catch what it says. fan goes loud before it cuts out tho

The loud fan noise before it cuts out is a strong clue: the hob’s internal temperature protection has likely triggered because it got too hot. This usually happens for one of two reasons. First, if the cooling vents are blocked by dust or grease (or if there isn't enough airflow around the unit), the whole hob overheats and shuts down to protect itself. Second, if you were using a very small pan on a large zone, the heat can’t spread properly and the sensor for that specific area gets too hot. To narrow this down:
1. When it switches off, check the vents (usually along the front edge or sides). Are they clear of dust/grease?
2. Which specific zone was active when it cut out, and what size/shape pan were you using on it? If the vents are blocked, cleaning them may solve it. If a small pan was used, try a larger one next time. If the vents are clear and the pans are correct, we’ll need to look at whether the fan itself is failing or if there’s an internal sensor issue.
dont know where the vents are, its a built in hob. big front zone mostly, on high/boost, proper induction pans. started after new drawer unit fitted under it last month tho

The fact that this started right after the new drawer unit was fitted is the key clue. Built-in induction hobs generate a lot of heat at high power and rely on airflow around them to cool down. If the new cabinetry has squeezed the space or blocked the vents, the hob will overheat and shut itself off within minutes to protect itself. Please check two things:
1. Is there still a gap (at least 2-3cm) between the bottom/sides of the hob and the new drawer unit? If it's touching or very tight, that's likely the cause.
2. Are the vents (usually along the front edge under the lip) clear of dust? If you find the space is too tight or blocked, widening the gap or cleaning the vents should fix it. If there is plenty of clearance and the vents are clean, then the internal cooling fan may have failed or become obstructed by debris over time, which would require an engineer to replace.
not pulling the drawer out or looking under the hob, not a diy person. just tell me if its the gap or a dodgy fan and who to call

It is probably the gap (blocked airflow) causing the hob to overheat and shut down, rather than a dodgy fan. The timing—starting right after the new drawer unit was fitted—is the giveaway. Induction hobs need air to cool themselves; if that space is tight or blocked, it overheats within minutes on high power. Since you are not DIY, do not try to pull the hob out or dismantle anything yourself. You need a qualified engineer to check the installation clearance and, if necessary, adjust the housing or replace the fan. Please call an appliance repair engineer or your kitchen fitter (if they still offer aftercare) to inspect the ventilation gap around the hob.

candidates: Overheating protection triggered (cooling fan failure or blocked vents) (high)
Power module overheating due to pan misuse or incorrect cookware (medium)
Faulty temperature sensor or main PCB (low)
